B.23.title: Minimum character depth, minimum unit-witness length and Selmer dimension agree up to p - 1
B.23.statement: For every good prime p >= 5 let d_p := dim_{F_p} Sel_p(E/Q); let r_p be the minimum number of distinct Kato primes supporting a mod-p unit Kurihara quantity (B.21); and let h_p be the minimum lambda-valuation (lambda = zeta_p - 1) of chi(theta_K), where theta_K is the full Bullach-Honnor-normalized Mazur-Tate element of a real cyclic degree-p field K at its actual conductor prime to pN and chi is a faithful character (h_p = +infinity is allowed). Then min(h_p, p - 1) = min(r_p, p - 1) = min(d_p, p - 1). Consequently, for this rank-two E and every good p >= 5: h_p < 4 <=> h_p = 2 <=> r_p = 2 <=> d_p <= 3 <=> Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity] = 0.

The criterion is sufficient only: no converse from $\Sha(E/\Q)[p^\infty]=0$ to the existence of such a character value is claimed here. The converse holds by \cid{B.23} (derived 2026-09-30); see Research record~\ref{thm:cmp}. It has not been evaluated at any $p\ge53$.

\subsection{Depth, witness length and Selmer dimension}\label{subsec:cmp}
For a good prime $p\ge5$ put $d_p=\dim_{\F_p}\Sel_p(E/\Q)$, let $r_p$ be as in Research record~\ref{thm:rp}, and let $h_p$ be the minimum of $v_{\zeta_p-1}(\chi(\theta_K^{\mathrm{MT}}))$ over the real cyclic extensions $K/\Q$ of degree $p$ at their actual conductors prime to $pN$ and over the faithful characters $\chi$ of $\Gal(K/\Q)$, where $\theta_K^{\mathrm{MT}}$ is the full Bullach--Honnor element; $h_p=+\infty$ is allowed.

\begin{researchrecord}[\cid{B.23}; written deduction from a preprint theorem; derived by ChatGPT Pro (OpenAI) and independently checked by Codex (OpenAI), with a cross-family check by Claude (Anthropic); not a human review; not formalized]\label{thm:cmp}
For every good prime $p\ge5$,
\[
\min(h_p,p-1)=\min(r_p,p-1)=\min(d_p,p-1).
\]
Consequently, for every good prime $p\ge5$,
\[
h_p<4\iff h_p=2\iff r_p=2\iff d_p\le3\iff\Sha(E/\Q)[p^\infty]=0 .
\]
\end{researchrecord}
This is an equivalence between existence statements. It does not say that a preselected field, or every field, attains depth two. It supplies no witness, no new vanishing prime and no upper bound. The strict inequality $<4$ and the cap $p-1$ are part of the statement. The proof applies Theorem~1.4(b) of \cite{bh} over the real abelian $p$-extensions $L$ of conductor prime to $pN$, with Fitting base change and a minimal presentation over the local ring $\F_p[\Gal(L/\Q)]$: since $E(L)[p]=0$, this gives $\theta_L\bmod p\in J^{d_p}$ for the augmentation ideal $J$. The conductor norm relation \cite[Prop.~2.4]{bh}, whose factor at a Kato prime is $-(u-1)^2/u\in J^2$, then identifies the degree-$d_p$ initial form at a minimum unit witness as $\delta_n\prod T_i$. Coefficients divisible by $p$ have valuation at least $p-1$, which is why the equality is capped. Research record~\ref{thm:depth} is the direction $h_p<4\Rightarrow\Sha(E/\Q)[p^\infty]=0$; the converse comes from the following bridge.

\begin{researchrecord}[\cid{B.24}; written deduction from a preprint theorem; conditional; derived by ChatGPT Pro (OpenAI) and independently checked by Codex (OpenAI), with a cross-family check by Claude (Anthropic); not a human review; not formalized]\label{thm:bridge}
Let $p\ge5$ be a good prime, let $q_1\ne q_2$ be Kato primes for $p$, and suppose that $\delta_{q_1q_2}$ is a mod-$p$ unit. Let $L$ be the $C_p^2$ compositum of the degree-$p$ subfields of $\Q(\mu_{q_1})$ and $\Q(\mu_{q_2})$, and let $J=(T_1,T_2)$ be the augmentation ideal of $\F_p[\Gal(L/\Q)]$. In the total-real-period normalization,
\[
\theta_L\equiv\delta_{q_1q_2}\,T_1T_2\pmod{p,\ J^3}.
\]
Every cyclic degree-$p$ quotient of $L$ that is nontrivial on both inertia groups (the diagonal quotient is one) has actual conductor $q_1q_2$, and each of its faithful characters has exact depth $2$.
\end{researchrecord}
The antecedent is a sufficient witness, not an established fact; no two-prime unit witness is supplied here. Here $\delta$ uses the symbol of Castella--Sano normalized by $\Omega_E^+=2\omega_1$, which is one half of the production symbol for this seed.

## V026-D addendum: the depth–length–Selmer comparison (content and stamp commits on `v0.2.6-bank`)

A follow-on on the same branch before any v0.2.6 push, governed by
`evidence/src/BSD_SEED_V026D_COMPARISON_TASK_2026-09-30/inputs/SCOPE_V026D.md`. It records one checked comparison. It
supplies no witness, no new vanishing prime and no upper bound. B.20 and B.21 are unchanged. B.22's statement, grades
and provenance are unchanged, apart from the qualification in item 3.

1. **B.23 (THEOREM; PROVED_WRITTEN, IMPORTED_PREPRINT; `thm:cmp`).** For every good p ≥ 5,
   min(h_p, p−1) = min(r_p, p−1) = min(d_p, p−1). Hence h_p < 4 ⟺ h_p = 2 ⟺ r_p = 2 ⟺ d_p ≤ 3 ⟺ Sha[p^∞] = 0.
   - Here d_p = dim_{F_p} Sel_p(E/Q), r_p is as in B.21, and h_p is the least λ-depth of a faithful character value of
     the full BH element of a real cyclic degree-p field at its actual conductor prime to pN (+∞ allowed).
   - Its three mandatory scope sentences are verbatim in the claim and in §9.2.
   - Inputs: BH Hyp 1.2, Thm 1.4(b), Def 2.2 and Prop 2.4 (a_q − u − u⁻¹); B.20; B.21; E(L)[p] = 0; Fitting base
     change; minimal presentations over F_p[G]; the cap p − 1.
2. **B.24 (CONDITIONAL; `thm:bridge`).** If δ_{q₁q₂} is a mod-p unit for Kato primes q₁ ≠ q₂, then
   θ_L ≡ δ_{q₁q₂}·T₁T₂ (mod p, J³) on the C_p² compositum. Every cyclic quotient that is nontrivial on both inertia
   groups has actual conductor q₁q₂ and exact depth 2.
   - The antecedent is a sufficient witness, not an established fact.
   - δ uses the Castella–Sano symbol with Ω_E⁺ = 2ω₁, which is one half of the production symbol for this seed.
3. **B.22's qualification (from the pre-check of the bank, addendum 33).**
   - The clause "and no such value has been computed at any prime" was false against the release's own S.17-47, and so
     was the README's "no value computed".
   - At each p = 17, …, 47, S.17-47 certifies C₀ = C₁ = 0 and C₂ ≢ 0 (mod p) at a singleton ℓ ∤ pN with v_p(ℓ−1) = 1.
     For the real degree-p subfield of Q(μ_ℓ), that gives a character value of depth exactly 2, up to p-adic units
     (the period factor 2; θ ↦ θ^# changes C₁ by a sign and C₂ by C₁).
   - The qualification now reads "…is claimed here. The converse holds by B.23 (derived 2026-09-30). It has not been
     evaluated at any p ≥ 53." The README row reads "not evaluated at p ≥ 53; converse: B.23".
   - No claim identifying S.17-47 with B.22 is added.
4. **The current known frontier** (O.1, §11, README) replaces the v0.2.6 wording, verbatim from the scope:

   > Current known frontier for the uniform part of FIN on good primes: one finite set S ⊇ {2, 3, 2243, 4547, 5843} with dim_{F_p} Sel_p(E/Q) ≤ 3 for every p ∉ S, or any independently proved equivalent criterion. By B.21–B.23 this is equivalent, prime by prime, to a two-prime mod-p unit Kurihara witness. It is also equivalent to a faithful character value, of depth strictly below four, of the full BH element of a real cyclic degree-p field at its actual conductor prime to pN. Fields, conductors and estimates may depend on p.
